# lookout audit ai

Inference-workload security and scheduling posture across workload templates: serving Services in namespaces with no ingress NetworkPolicy isolating the model endpoint, hostNetwork on accelerator workloads, hostPath model-cache volumes, default ServiceAccount token automount on accelerator workloads, and unpinned model-loader or inference images. Scope with --namespace, -A, or --workload.

MCP tool: `k8s_audit_ai` (MCP profile: `audit`)

## Usage

    lookout audit ai [flags]

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--skip-system-namespaces` | — | skip system namespaces matching the active posture policy's system_namespaces patterns |
| `--policy` | — | path to a YAML posture policy file |
| `--profile` | — | built-in posture profile: default\|strict\|onboarding\|gke-autopilot |
| `--only` | — | comma-separated check kind or kind/reason globs to run exclusively |
| `--skip` | — | comma-separated check kind or kind/reason globs to skip |
| `--min-severity` | — | minimum finding severity to emit: info\|warning\|critical |
| `--set` | — | comma-separated check parameter overrides (<kind>.<param>=<val>) |

## Common flags (every lookout command)

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--namespace` | — | limit the scan to one namespace |
| `-A` | — | scan all namespaces |
| `--workload` | — | target one workload as <Kind>/<namespace>/<name>, e.g. Deployment/prod/api |
| `--since` | — | how far back to look (0 = command default) |
| `--format` | logfmt | output format: logfmt\|json (one record per line either way) |
| `--timeout` | 30s | abort the invocation after this long (exit 1) |
| `--kubeconfig` | — | path to a kubeconfig file, instead of $KUBECONFIG / ~/.kube/config |
| `--kubeconfig-dir` | — | directory of kubeconfig files to fan out across (mutually exclusive with --kubeconfig); each finding is stamped with cluster=<label> and the summary reports clusters=<n> |
| `--context` | — | kubeconfig context to read, instead of its current-context. Selects a cluster for THIS invocation only — nothing is written back — so concurrent invocations can target different clusters. Reported as context=<name> in the summary line |
| `--contexts` | — | comma-separated kubeconfig contexts to fan out across, or '*' for every context in the selected kubeconfig(s) (mutually exclusive with --context); each finding is stamped with cluster=<label> and the summary reports clusters=<n> |
| `--concurrency` | 4 | maximum concurrent cluster executions when fanning out with --contexts or --kubeconfig-dir |
| `--exemptions` | — | path to a git-reviewed exemption file (YAML); covered findings are ANNOTATED with their reason and expiry and counted as exempt=<n> in the summary, never dropped |

## Finding kinds

Every `kind=` this command can emit, and the severities it carries them at. Nothing else appears in its output; a kind absent from a run means the check looked and found nothing.

| Kind | Severity | Claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.ai_workload_exposure` | warning, info | an AI/inference workload has an unisolated serving Service, hostNetwork with accelerators, a hostPath model-cache mount, an automounted default ServiceAccount token, or an unpinned model-loader/inference container image |
| `read.unavailable` | info | a resource this command reads was refused (RBAC forbidden, e.g. Nodes, Secrets or RBAC objects under the built-in view role) or is not served, so the checks that need it did not run and their silence is not a clean bill; everything else was still verified. The message names the refused verb and resource, whether it is cluster-scoped, whether the built-in view role grants it, and the grant that fixes it; resource= carries the refused resource as resource[.group] — an explicit degradation record, never silence (§11) |

## Output fields

Beyond the shared envelope fields (`kind`, `severity`, `namespace`, `kind_of_object`, `name`, `reason`, `message`, `fingerprint`, `exempt_reason`, `exempt_expires`):

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `service` | Service(s) selecting the unisolated AI inference workload (ServingPortClusterWideNoNetPol) |
| `ports` | Service port(s) exposed without an ingress NetworkPolicy (ServingPortClusterWideNoNetPol) |
| `accelerator` | accelerator resource or node selector detected on the workload, when present |
| `volumes` | comma-separated name:path pairs (capped at 8) of hostPath volumes mounted by the AI workload (SharedModelCacheHostPath) |
| `service_account` | ServiceAccount name used by the AI workload (DefaultSAWithAccelerator) |
| `containers` | count of containers in the AI workload template with an unpinned image reference (UnpinnedModelLoaderImage) |
| `container_names` | comma-separated container names (capped at 8) with an unpinned image reference (UnpinnedModelLoaderImage) |
| `total_containers` | total containers (init + regular) in the AI workload template (UnpinnedModelLoaderImage) |
| `ai_workloads` | summary-line note: count of AI/inference workload templates identified in the scan scope |
| `skipped_system_namespaces` | summary note: distinct system namespaces skipped under `--skip-system-namespaces` |
| `resource` | read.unavailable: the resource that could not be read, as resource[.group] |

## Output contract

Output: one finding per line (logfmt; --format=json for one JSON object
per line), keys in fixed order; healthy resources emit nothing. The final
line is always the summary: scanned=<n> findings=<n> elapsed=<d> —
findings=0 with a summary present means "scanned and healthy"; a stream
without a summary line is void. Exit 0 data, 1 runtime error (diagnostics
on stderr only), 2 usage.

## Examples

```lookout
lookout audit ai -A
lookout audit ai --namespace=ml
lookout audit ai --workload=Deployment/ml/vllm-llama
```
